checks.rule: OS Net base-station coordinate standard errors are generally better than 0.008 m in plan.
OS Net base-station coordinate standard errors are generally better than 0.020 m in height.
OSTN15 defines OSGB36 National Grid in conjunction with OS Net stations.
Agreement between OSTN15 and old triangulation network stations is about 0.1 m RMS for Great Britain.
OSGM15 Great Britain vertical datum standard error is 0.008 m, excluding GNSS heighting error.
OSGM15 error and GNSS positional/heighting error are separate error components.
Do not treat GNSS/WGS84 coordinates as OSGB36 National Grid coordinates without an explicit transformation.
Require vertical-datum provenance before comparing heights from separate sources.
Keep GNSS heighting error separate from OSGM15 model error in the uncertainty budget.
Do not use legacy triangulation agreement as parcel-boundary precision evidence.
Reject mixed-datum height differences when one endpoint lacks an ODN-compatible transformation path.
Promote a measured height-difference row only after horizontal CRS and vertical datum checks both pass.
